liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Reviewer notes Deadbase does not list Morning Dew for this date, and questions its origin; Reviewer's tape lacked Dew; in the Dew, Jerry's guitar and vocal are low in the levels [16][17]
- **New Potato Canboose** (2 reviews): Source highlights the sequence of New Potato into Cross-Eyed into Spanish Jam as a rare combination; Reviewer says this may be the best New Potato ever played [9][12]
- **Alligator** (1 review, 1 other source): There is a cut in Alligator, missing a passage resembling the Mountain Jam; it can be patched from the Anthem album; All circulating copies have a cut in the jam [3][11]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer describes this Dark Star as embryonic [10]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight features an unusual jazzy vocal jam [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Born Cross-eyed**: rare: 14 archived performances [21]
- **Spanish Inquisition**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **Alligator Underwater Feedback**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **Alligator Underwater Feedback**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-02-14.sbd.douglas-cleef.2267.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 170 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1968-02-14.sbd.winters.89437.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 125 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Garcia and Weir were in and out of tune throughout the show, with pitch varying within songs [2]
- **gd68-02-14.sbd.kaplan.15640.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 126 min; rated 4.6/5 by 72 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard good for 1968; Soundboard quality is fabulous, unusual for 1968; Alligator cut should be patched from Anthem of the Sun; FM broadcast is slightly louder; the second Alligator portion has an obvious, painful pitch error [9][12][18][20]
- **gd1968-02-14.sbd.miller.89676.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 124 min; rated 3.67/5 by 21 [4]

## Around the show

- Pigpen's calliope-like organ still dominates, with crunchy Garcia and Weir guitars, frantic Lesh bass, and interlocking drummers [10]
- Less technically polished than 1972-73 Dead, but a peak of the acid rock era rather than cerebral [10]
- Reviewer ranks it among the best shows of 1968, possibly the best [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-02-14.sbd.douglas-cleef.2267.shnf**: transferred by Garrett Van Cleef; source: MR>DAT>DAT>CD>EAC>SHN [1]. Also: Copy credited to Jim Douglas, tracks arranged by Garrett Van Cleef; some portions may come from the FM broadcast; Encore placed on Disc 1 to keep sets continuous; can move to Disc 2 on 80-minute CDs [1]
- **gd1968-02-14.sbd.winters.89437.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Dave Winters; source: SBD>MR>DAT>CD>EAC>SHN>WAV>Cool Edit Pro v2.0>FLAC [2]. Also: Gator Jam splice patched from Anthem CD reissue; pitch issues fixed using Cool Edit Pro, encoded to FLAC [2]
- **gd68-02-14.sbd.kaplan.15640.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by AJL, Tony C., and Seth Kaplan; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Missing Alligator portion can be patched in from Anthem of the Sun [18]
- **gd1968-02-14.sbd.miller.89676.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (8 Track) Master Reel -> Dat -> CD -> FLAC [4]. Also: Remaster of shnid 89437: Alligator Jam patch fixed, levels adjusted, DC offset corrected, patch source pitch-corrected [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by zoooma (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead concert poster - 2/14/68 Carouse…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/zoooma/2264649871/) [22]
- Poster by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/zoooma/2264649871/) [23]
